aoi_name: Liwa (eastern crescent: Wadhil / Mawsil), southern Abu Dhabi

baseline.note: velocities from the Landsat 8/9 OLI network (12 November scenes, 66 pairs); the Landsat 7 scenes (2000-11-27, 2001-11-30) are used only as a long-baseline check

speed_note: speeds are of the 3521 dune windows (480 m) with detected motion (93.1 % of 3782 valid); the other 261 move slower than their detection limit (median 0.49 m/yr) and are not in these statistics. Max detected 5.40 m/yr. uncertainty_myr = median calibrated 1-sigma per component.
wind_agreement_note: mean |heading - RDD| over detected windows, RDD 145.3 deg (MERRA-2 2000-2024). The regime is close to unimodal (RDP/DP 0.594): the field-median heading 165.8 deg is 8.3 deg from the strongest sand-moving mode (toward 157.5 deg) and 20.5 deg from RDD; per-window median difference 20.4 deg. Year-to-year field speeds follow the MERRA-2 drift (r 0.432).

published.reference: Lorenz, Radebaugh, Barnes & Turtle, EGU2016-9369; Lorenz & Radebaugh 2015 (Planetary Dunes Workshop 8003); Pugh, Glennie & Williams 1993 (AAPG abstract)
published.their_value: ~0.1 m/yr for the 50-80 m Liwa megadunes (a field inference from overrun date palms, abstracts only); the smaller northern dunes 'migrate southward more rapidly than the draa' (no number)
published.our_value: megadune bodies: not measured (the body-scale matcher failed its known-shift test, notebook 02 section 15b), and with the registration reference itself uncertain by about +-0.10 m/yr their motion is below what this method can resolve here; small dunes and bedforms: 1.41 m/yr median toward 166 deg (2013-2025), 1.33-1.50 m/yr depending on the registration reference
published.note: Consistent with the published direction (south-south-east) and with small dunes moving much faster than the megadunes are reported to move, but not a test of the 0.1 m/yr: that rate is below what this method can resolve here, and the megadune bodies are not measured.

second_dataset.their_value: HLS S30 (Sentinel-2, independent): field median 0.466 m/yr toward 171.5 deg; per-window correlation with Landsat r = 0.423 (E), 0.726 (N); its detection limit 0.631 m/yr, motion detected in 37.8 % of windows. HLS L30 (same Landsat instruments, not independent): 0.571 m/yr toward 169.7 deg, r = 0.444/0.724
second_dataset.our_value: Landsat pan 15 m over the same years: field median 1.313 m/yr toward 164.0 deg (S30 years); 1.382 m/yr toward 166.1 deg (L30 years)
second_dataset.note: HLS S30 (Sentinel-2, independent geolocation) and L30 (same Landsat instruments) are registered on the same two canopy-free references as Landsat, on their own 30 m grids (S30: mean of hard_outside_farms (68 windows) and bare_in_farms (1562 windows) on HLS's own 30 m grid; L30: mean of hard_outside_farms (58 windows) and bare_in_farms (1279 windows) on HLS's own 30 m grid). S30: field headings 7.5 deg apart, r 0.423 E / 0.726 N, 0.466 vs 1.313 m/yr. L30: headings 3.6 deg apart, 0.571 vs 1.382 m/yr. In all three sensors the farm canopy drifts against canopy-free ground by ~0.2-0.45 m/yr toward the north-north-west.

data_handling.display_only_frames: 11 Landsat 7 frames (2002-10-16, 2003-11-20, 2004-10-21, 2005-11-09, 2006-10-11, 2007-10-14, 2008-11-17, 2009-10-19, 2010-10-06, 2011-11-10, 2012-11-12; off-month: 2002-10-16, 2004-10-21, 2006-10-11, 2007-10-14, 2009-10-19, 2010-10-06) are shown on the timeline as images only, scan-line gaps left as no-data; they are not used in any number in this file (see frames/manifest.json observed_display_only).
data_handling.notes: 4 November candidate scenes rejected in notebook 01 (cloud/shadow/haze/coverage; listed in pipeline/outputs/liwa/scene_rejections.csv); Landsat 7 used only before the 31 May 2003 SLC failure. Clouds/shadows: Landsat QA_PIXEL bits 0-4 (dilated 1 px), HLS Fmask bits 1-3. Of 10403 tracking windows, 3290 lie outside the box and 3307 are mostly non-dune (vegetation, WorldCover, OSM, hand-drawn change areas); of the 3806 dune windows 0.63 % had too few valid pairs. Window-pair observations rejected: 4.14 % (weak match below the false-match threshold, displacement beyond the reliable range, network outliers).

limits: Detected dune windows move a median 1.41 m/yr (10-90 %: 0.79-2.25, max 5.40) toward 166 deg; 7 % of valid dune windows move below the detection limit (median 0.49 m/yr).

These speeds are relative to a registration reference that is itself uncertain. The farm canopy, the only stable ground used before, drifts toward the north-north-west (toward the anti-sun direction) and is not used. The speeds are measured against the mean of two canopy-free references (paved roads and buildings outside the farms; bare ground inside the farms), which differ by 1.50 vs 1.33 m/yr in the median dune speed. Half their difference (0.10 m/yr per component) is included in the uncertainty and the detection limit. On the farms alone the median would have been 1.74 m/yr.

Megadune bodies (up to ~110 m of relief) are not measured: the body-scale matcher failed its known-shift test, so no body speed is reported. The motion in the velocity grid, the dune polygons and the reach years is that of the small dunes and the bedforms riding over the megadunes, not of the megadunes themselves.

Reach years forecast the migration of dune forms (slip-face advance), not wind-blown sand crossing a road, which happens wherever a road borders loose sand, whatever the dunes do (see borders_free_sand in targets.geojson).
At the median speed (~1.4 m/yr) one 15 m pixel is about a decade of motion, so reach years for targets near the sand carry an edge uncertainty of +-7.5 m plus the outline uncertainty of the target.
Most targets are not reached by 2050; targets flagged 'sand at edge now' already have migrating sand within that edge uncertainty.
The projection is advection along the measured 2013-2025 motion, assuming those conditions continue; it does not model dune deformation, merging, splitting or growth.
Vegetation, windbreaks, sand fences, levelling, construction and climate change alter the outcome; many farm edges here are walled.
Motion is measured in 480 m windows: it is the motion of the small dunes (spacing ~85-115 m) and sand sheets inside, not of a single dune body.
Only 17 dunes (13-31 m high) are outlined from NASADEM (February 2000) at bedform scale; they are medium dunes, mostly in the northern field, not megadunes.

The second dataset confirms the direction but not the speed: HLS S30 and L30 (30 m red band, registered on the same canopy-free references) give 0.47 and 0.57 m/yr against 1.31-1.38 m/yr for Landsat pan over the same years. At the other two sites L30 agrees with pan within ~0.1 m/yr. Until this is understood, the pan speed magnitude here has no independent confirmation.
The published ~0.1 m/yr for the megadunes is a field inference far below what this method can resolve here: no numeric comparison is possible.
MERRA-2 wind is a ~0.5 x 0.625 deg reanalysis of hourly means; absolute drift potential is approximate.
Farm targets are vegetated plots (HLS NDVI, last year) plus OSM farmland; built-up targets are OSM buildings and residential areas; unmapped or abandoned plots are not targets.
Results are valid for this box (the eastern Liwa crescent, not Liwa town) and 2013-2025 only; nothing outside the box is assessed.

threat.reach_definition: Migrating dune sand (free sand inside a window whose dune-form migration is detected), carried along its measured heading at its measured speed, arrives at the edge of the target footprint (road: OSM centre line +- class half width incl. shoulders; farm: HLS vegetated outline; built-up: OSM outline).
excludes: wind-blown sand crossing or settling on a target
motion below the detection limit (no direction: never a hit)
dune deformation, merging, growth, levelling or stabilisation
threat.speeds: median = measured window speed v; fast = v + sigma; slow = v - sigma (sigma = calibrated per-component 1-sigma; 84th/16th percentiles of the speed)
threat.years: hit_year_min = floor(t0 + gap_lo / fast); hit_year_max = ceil(t0 + gap_hi / slow); gap = distance from the source pixel centre to the footprint along the heading minus 7.5 m, +-(7.5 m + outline uncertainty: roads/buildings 5 m, farms 15 m); t0 = 2025-11-08; earliest over all sand reaching the target; null if the fast case does not arrive by 2100

confirmation.rule: speed agrees if a check's field-median speed is within 15% of Landsat's over the same windows and years; heading agrees if the field-median headings differ by <= 20 deg (Landsat 7: per-window east and north correlations both >= 0.8). confirmed = the independent Sentinel-2 check (HLS S30) agrees; partly_confirmed = only the partly independent Landsat 7 long baseline agrees; not_confirmed = neither. HLS L30 uses the same Landsat 8/9 instruments and is shown for context only.
